stories.title: China, Russia and US agree peace declaration with no mention of Ukraine and Iran wars
stories.dek: Xi, Putin and Trump outline priorities that include UN reform, boosting oil supplies and ‘protection of diplomatic immunity’ China, Russia and the US say they have agreed a peace statement after an un…
stories.content:
Vladimir Putin, Xi Jinping and Donald Trump at the trilateral talks in China. Photograph: White House Office/APAImages/Shutterstock View image in fullscreen Vladimir Putin, Xi Jinping and Donald Trump at the trilateral talks in China. Photograph: White House Office/APAImages/Shutterstock Apec summit China, Russia and US agree peace declaration with no mention of Ukraine and Iran wars Xi, Putin and Trump outline priorities that include UN reform, boosting oil supplies and ‘protection of diplomatic immunity’

China, Russia and the US say they have agreed a peace statement after an unprecedented trilateral summit, but the declaration made no mention of the wars in Ukraine and Iran caused by two of the participants.

The declaration on Thursday also outlined a set of priorities that included changing the UN, boosting oil supplies and what it said was the protection of diplomatic immunity.

The statement affirmed that “a nuclear war cannot be won and must not be fought”, but stopped short of suggesting the beginnings of a framework for denuclearisation.

10:23 Troublesome trio: Trump, Xi and Putin hold historic meeting - The Latest The meeting between Xi Jinping, Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump has dominated the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) summit this week, with China, the host, promising it would be “groundbreaking”.

“We are really making history,” Trump told Xi and Putin at the start of the meeting. “No peace was ever forged by declining opportunities for engagement.”

Press conference following the end of Apec summit – watch live Putin told a press conference later that the three men had had a “free discussion” and now had a “mutual understanding”.

Some had hopes that the talks, which lasted about one hour and 20 minutes, could be used to discuss reductions in arms between the world’s three largest nuclear powers. Beijing has previously rebuffed Trump’s advances to join such talks, pointing to the larger US and Russian stockpiles. On Thursday, though, Xi called for nuclear weapons to “be completely prohibited and thoroughly destroyed over time to make the world free of [them]”.

The language of the declaration around nuclear war is the same as that previously issued by the five permanent members of the UN security council, which includes France and the UK.

View image in fullscreen Vladimir Putin shakes hands with Donald Trump in front of other world leaders at the Apec summit in Shenzhen, China. Photograph: Lukas Coch/AAP “The real test will be whether the three countries follow through on their stated commitment to discuss nuclear risk reduction and preventing nuclear proliferation,” said Patricia Kim, an expert on Chinese foreign policy at the Brookings Institution, a US thinktank. Even the suggestion that China would engage was significant, said Yun Sun, a senior fellow at the Stimson Center.

stories.title: Protesters call for regime change in Iran following deadly crash that killed 13 oil and gas workers
stories.dek: The demonstrations carry particular significance because Abdanan was previously a flashpoint during Iran's nationwide anti-government protests earlier this year.
stories.content:
Thousands of protesters gathered in western Iran renewing calls for a regime change within the nation following a deadly bus crash that killed 13 oil and gas workers.

The unrest broke out this week in the city of Abdanan, in the Ilam province near the Iraqi border, where members of Iran’s Kurdish minority demanded answers and accountability over Saturday’s fatal accident.

The demonstration eventually grew to around 1,000 people, with the event rapidly spiraling into an anti-regime protest.

The streets were eventually filled with chants of “Death to the dictator,” along with calls for Iran to return to the Pahlavi monarchy, which was ousted during the 1979 revolution.

Abdanan is a reminder that the Islamic Republic sits on top of a dormant volcano,” Iranian-American journalist Lisa Daftari told Fox News Digital.

“These uprisings start with different catalysts, and in this case it was a local grievance, but they always arrive at the same conclusion,” she said.

“The slogans we hear are ‘Death to the Dictator’ and ‘Javid Shah,’ not complaints about a policy,” Daftari added. “They are an indictment of the entire system, top to bottom.”

Mojtaba Najafi, a France-based political analyst, echoed the current uneasiness inside the country, warning that the public was “like a powder keg” that could be set off by any incident.

But any protest that gets big enough will be wiped out by the government forces, especially amid the ongoing war with the US, Najafi told Radio Free Europe .

“In a state of war or near-war, the government uses more force against its opponents, and the level of repression will also rise,” he said.

Morning Report delivers the latest news, videos, photos and more.

By clicking above you agree to the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy .

Abdanan, a town of about 24,000 people, was one of the center points of the January anti-regime protests and home to some of the most violent crackdowns by Iran’s security forces.

The vast majority of the Ilam province is made out of Iran’s Kurdish minority, a group that has long sought independence from Iran.

The US was reported to be arming the Kurds to lead a regime change in Iran earlier this year, but the White House has denied the claims.

Like with the anti-regime protests that broke out in January , Tehran sent out its forces to crush the demonstrators on Tuesday.

stories.title: Inside SMAC: India’s single malt club of whisky nerds
stories.dek: India’s whisky nerds have a clubhouse.
stories.content:

At the India Rare Spirits whisky tasting session in Goa in September organised by Single Malt Amateur Club and Diageo | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement

A glass of single malt whisky is personal. It does not speak to you or alert you of the world’s distress. It simply waits as time languishes between sips, hoping that your own story unravels in its midst.

These are not Dr Anupam Dutta’s (Doctor of Medicine, Assam Medical College, Dibrugarh ), exact words, but you get the drift. Dr Dutta calls a glass of peated whisky, the golden liquid. According to him, the ideal way to enjoy single malt is a 60ml pour in a Glencairn glass (preferably an aged Lagavulin) as jazz notes sway in the background. A good book or a painting will build the evening’s essence.

While drinking that exact one glass, Dr Dutta says attention is mandatory. After all, years of effort have gone into not just making but aging malted barley in sophisticated distilleries from around the world so that it lands up in Dibrugarh for the evening.

“In India, most people drink to get high. After learning to appreciate single malt over the last two decades, I’ve realised that I rarely ever drink to get drunk. Our taste receptors go for a toss after the second glass, so it gets hard to identify the notes. I like to be academic, geeky even. It is why I travel for single malt,” he says.

Anupam Dutta is not alone in this pursuit though. Since 2016, he has been a member of Single Malt Amateur Club (SMAC), a Bengaluru-based whisky appreciation club that seems to have aficionados with noses both trained and untrained. Besides hosting events around the country in collaboration with top brands, members of the club (the number stands at around 7,500) meet on the regular in their respective cities and through the club’s collaborative events to put all their theoretical knowledge to practical experiments. The club’s recommendations are particularly sought after because of its many competent members who are stacked with opinions about the mostly amber-looking drink (the spectrum ranges from clear to mahogany/deep brown. Don’t sue me, please).

stories.title: Google is putting AI chats right on the homepage
stories.dek: Google is updating its homepage to include AI searches.
stories.content:
You can now view your recent AI searches by opening the sidebar on Google’s homepage.

You can now view your recent AI searches by opening the sidebar on Google’s homepage.

Google is updating its homepage to include AI searches. In a post on X , Google’s vice president of product, Robby Stein, shows how you can now open a collapsible sidebar to view and continue your AI chats.

Based on the GIF shared by Stein, it looks like you can open the sidebar by clicking the gray bar that appears on the left side of your screen. From there, Google will show a list of the searches you’ve made using AI Mode, along with the ability to start a new thread, search your threads, or connect a Gemini Notebook.

It’s yet another big change for Google’s homepage, which has long presented you with a single bar to kick off your web search. The company brought its AI Mode button to its search bar last year, which opens up a chatbot-like search experience within Google. In May, Google updated its search box to accommodate longer queries and added AI-powered autocomplete.

Stein says Google is rolling out the option because “people are coming to Search with more questions that aren’t just one and done,” adding that “in testing, this sidebar made a big difference for making progress & continuing to explore the web.” The new homepage is rolling out globally on desktop.

stories.title: Scientists recreate a bizarre quantum effect that stops a particle cold
stories.dek: Oxford physicists have recreated a bizarre quantum effect in which a particle responds to a magnetic field without ever traveling through it.
stories.content:
A particle does not have to pass through a magnetic field to be influenced by it. That surprising feature of quantum physics has now been recreated by researchers at the University of Oxford, who used a hybrid quantum computer to demonstrate how an invisible magnetic influence can bring a simulated particle's movement to a complete stop.

The experiment reproduced a phenomenon known as the Aharonov-Bohm effect, in which a charged particle traveling around a region containing magnetic flux experiences a measurable change in its quantum state, even though its path never takes it through the magnetic field itself.

The Oxford team achieved this using a quantum system that combines qubits, the basic units of quantum information, with quantum oscillators, which represent vibrating motion. Their findings, published in Nature Physics , demonstrate how this combination could help scientists investigate fundamental interactions between matter and fields that are increasingly difficult to simulate using conventional computers.

In everyday physics, a charged particle responds to the electric and magnetic fields it encounters. Quantum mechanics, however, reveals that particles can behave in ways that have no straightforward counterpart in our ordinary experience.

In 1959, physicists Yakir Aharonov and David Bohm predicted that a charged particle could be affected by magnetic flux even if it traveled entirely outside the region containing the magnetic field. Rather than experiencing a conventional magnetic force along its path, the particle would undergo a change in its quantum phase.

Quantum phase describes an aspect of a particle's wave behavior that influences how different possible paths interfere with one another. Although the phase itself is not directly visible, differences in phase can produce measurable effects.

The prediction became known as the Aharonov-Bohm effect and was eventually verified in experiments involving real electrons. It remains one of the clearest demonstrations that the quantum world operates according to rules that go beyond the familiar laws of classical physics.

Researchers are now exploring how this phenomenon behaves in more complex theoretical systems known as lattice gauge theories.

These theories describe how matter interacts with fields associated with fundamental forces. They represent space as a grid, with matter located at individual points and fields associated with the connections between them. Such models are particularly important in particle physics and high-energy physics, where scientists study the basic particles and interactions that make up the universe.

stories.title: Eastern Mediterranean Maritime Agreements and Regional Energy Corridors
stories.dek: A multi-perspective assessment of offshore natural gas transit frameworks, maritime boundary negotiations, and regional stability.
stories.content:
The Eastern Mediterranean basin continues to navigate complex multilateral diplomatic engagements balancing offshore energy exploration with sovereign boundary delimitation. High-level delegations from regional coastal states and European partners are refining frameworks that align pipeline routes with equitable maritime economic zones.

Key Perspectives & Strategic Dimensions:
1. Energy Transit Security: Multilateral agreements between Mediterranean states prioritize uninterrupted transit of natural gas to Southern European ports, diversifying continental supply lines.
2. Maritime Boundary Delimitation: Diplomatic mediators emphasize that long-term maritime stability necessitates transparent dispute-resolution mechanisms that account for sovereign continental shelf claims.
3. Regional Economic Interdependence: Joint infrastructure investments in subsea interconnectors create economic mutual interest, offering pragmatic stabilization incentives across diverse stakeholders.
stories.whyItMatters: Directly impacts the economic stability, energy infrastructure, and security landscape across the Levant and Mediterranean.

stories.title: Sub-Microsecond Spin Dynamics in Diamond NV Centers: Benchmarking Cavity QED and Coherence Limits
stories.dek: Mitigating dipolar spin-spin dephasing and hyperfine bath interactions in dense diamond NV ensembles via Floquet driving.
stories.content:
Nitrogen-vacancy (NV) color centers in diamond remain the preeminent solid-state platform for room-temperature quantum metrology and nanoscale magnetic resonance. Scaling from isolated defects to dense ensembles requires overcoming collective dephasing from the surrounding 13C nuclear spin bath.

Recent breakthroughs utilizing microwave cavity coupling and Floquet dynamical decoupling extend the effective coherence time (T2*) by an order of magnitude.

Key Technical Highlights:
1. Cooperative Purcell Enhancement: Dense NV ensembles entering the collective strong coupling regime demonstrate cavity-mediated coherence preservation.
2. Suppression of Spin-Diffusion Loss: Operating within crystallographic symmetry subspaces eliminates cross-axis relaxation.
3. Room-Temperature Sensing: Sustained microsecond coherence enables sub-picotesla magnetic field sensitivities for single-cell NMR.
stories.whyItMatters: Informs room-temperature diamond quantum magnetometry, microwave cavity loading, and advanced Floquet decoupling protocols in spin dynamics.

stories.source: Innatera & Edge AI Insights • 5 min read
stories.title: Sub-Milliwatt Neuromorphic Microcontrollers Shift Real-Time AI Inference to the Edge
stories.dek: Spiking neural networks (SNNs) on silicon processors achieve microsecond response times at sub-milliwatt power budgets.
stories.content:
The paradigm of routing sensor telemetry to centralized cloud servers is rapidly transitioning to on-device neuromorphic microcontrollers. Utilizing event-driven spiking neural architectures, silicon accelerators process acoustic and vibration patterns with near-zero latency.

Key Highlights:
1. In-Memory Processing: Spiking architectures circumvent the classical von Neumann memory bottleneck, consuming less than 1 mW.
2. Zero Cloud Exposure: Sensitive sensor streams remain strictly local, guaranteeing privacy and continuous operation during network blackouts.
3. Predictive Maintenance: Deployed microcontrollers classify industrial vibrations and structural stress in real time.
stories.whyItMatters: Enables zero-latency, private, on-device anomaly detection and vibration monitoring without cloud roundtrips.

stories.title: Circadian Photonic Priming and Equanimity in Demanding Research
stories.dek: Aligning 90-minute ultradian deep work blocks with natural circadian rhythms and secular Buddhist non-reactivity.
stories.content:
Sustained high-level analytical performance requires deliberate biological pacing. Structuring the day around 90-minute ultradian cycles followed by brief decompression intervals prevents cognitive fatigue.

Core Evidence-Based Habits:
1. Photonic Lock: Direct outdoor light exposure within 45 minutes of waking aligns the suprachiasmatic nucleus master clock.
2. Ultradian Block: Dedicate the primary 9:00 AM - 10:30 AM window to pure theoretical derivation before checking correspondence.
3. Secular Equanimity (Dhammapada 81): 'Just as a solid rock is not shaken by the storm, even so the wise are not affected by praise or blame.'
stories.whyItMatters: Protects cognitive bandwidth and prevents attentional fragmentation during demanding laboratory derivations.

papers.title: Thermally Activated Magnetic Switching in Antiferromagnetic Van der Waals Trilayers Resolved by Single-Spin Diamond Magnetometry
papers.authors: Fabian A. Gerritsma, Roland W. Mulder, Balázs Nagyfalusi et al.
papers.tldr: Van der Waals magnets provide a versatile platform for exploring magnetic phenomena that emerge from reduced dimensionality, including layer-dependent magnetic ordering. Here, we use scanning nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond magnetometry to measure the magnetization of a trilayer of the A-type antiferromagnet CrPS$_4$, resolving its zero-field bistability between the up-down-up ($\uparrow\downarrow\uparrow$) and down-up-down ($\downarrow\uparrow\downarrow$) layer magnetization configurations.
takeaways: Van der Waals magnets provide a versatile platform for exploring magnetic phenomena that emerge from reduced dimensionality, including layer-dependent magnetic ordering.

Here, we use scanning nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond magnetometry to measure the magnetization of a trilayer of the A-type antiferromagnet CrPS$_4$, resolving its zero-field bistability between the up-down-up ($\uparrow\downarrow\uparrow$) and down-up-down ($\downarrow\uparrow\downarrow$) layer magnetization configurations.

Our results highlight the power of scanning NV magnetometry for the quantitative investigation of magnetization reversal in two-dimensional magnets, unraveling the magnetic phenomenology that emerges in low-dimensional systems.

papers.title: Bright and Uniform Silicon Carbide Nanophotonic Arrays for Scalable Nanoscale Quantum Sensing
papers.authors: Chenyang Liao, Chihang Luo, Xin Chen et al.
papers.tldr: Silicon carbide (SiC) spin defects are emerging as powerful platforms for nanoscale quantum sensing due to their near-surface stability, near-infrared emission, and CMOS compatibility. However, poor photon collection efficiency and the reliance on randomly distributed defects hinder the realization of practical, large-scale devices.
takeaways: Silicon carbide (SiC) spin defects are emerging as powerful platforms for nanoscale quantum sensing due to their near-surface stability, near-infrared emission, and CMOS compatibility.
Furthermore, we apply these devices to nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), successfully demonstrating external nanoscale nuclear-spin detection.
These results establish our SiC nanopillars as robust building blocks for scanning quantum probes and scalable sensor networks.

papers.title: Algorithmic Quantum Sensing
papers.authors: Ishaan Kannan, Aditi Venkatesh, Jordan Cotler
papers.tldr: We introduce a unified framework for sensing time-dependent fields through the lens of classical and quantum algorithms. First, we develop three pulse sequence protocols, namely randomized, matched, and pooled spectroscopy, which outperform established approaches such as dynamical decoupling across a wide range of tasks.
takeaways: First, we develop three pulse sequence protocols, namely randomized, matched, and pooled spectroscopy, which outperform established approaches such as dynamical decoupling across a wide range of tasks.
These protocols attain the optimal sensitivity for linear and nonlinear AC sensing on conventional spin or qubit platforms, improving existing devices by changing only their pulse sequences.

Our result provides the first asymptotic, beyond-quadratic quantum advantage in AC metrology when noise is aligned with the signal, proving that Lindblad span conditions do not apply to broadband quantum sensing.

papers.title: To predict or to persist: how decoherence shapes learning in a spin-qubit quantum reservoir
papers.tldr: In this work we investigate how dephasing and the choice of measured observables affect learning in a simulated six-qubit spin chain with Markovian dissipation and exact expectation-value readout. For externally driven nonlinear autoregressive moving-average signals, combining single- and two-qubit observables gives better predictions than a population-only readout at comparable polynomial feature counts.
takeaways: In this work we investigate how dephasing and the choice of measured observables affect learning in a simulated six-qubit spin chain with Markovian dissipation and exact expectation-value readout.
We do not find a clear systematic dependence of limit-cycle persistence on coherence across the reservoir ensemble.
We conclude that, within this simulated reservoir, the impact of coherence depends strongly on the task.

papers.title: Spin dynamics in disordered systems with generic spin-momentum couplings: A matrix-rational formulation
papers.tldr: We develop a microscopic framework for the disorder-averaged density-matrix dynamics of pseudospin-$1/2$ systems with anisotropic and nonlinear spin-momentum couplings. Starting from the Diffuson, we introduce a matrix-valued rational approximation for its frequency dependence that does not rely on a low-frequency or weak-coupling expansion.
takeaways: We develop a microscopic framework for the disorder-averaged density-matrix dynamics of pseudospin-$1/2$ systems with anisotropic and nonlinear spin-momentum couplings.

Comparisons with direct numerical simulations demonstrate quantitative agreement for both the post-quench spin dynamics and spin relaxation times across a broad range of coupling strengths, extending beyond the diffusive regime.
The matrix-rational formulation provides a unified description of ultrafast spin dynamics and long-time relaxation.
